missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Final crossing. Walk through the eighth torii — the one that does not exist yet. Trust the Kami way: perception shapes reality. Walk, and it becomes real.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: The Eighth Shadow — what the eighth torii would be if it formed without guidance. It is chaos given a gate-shape.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: The Eighth Shadow is what happens if the torii forms without guidance — chaos through a gate. Your passage is what guides it. Walk clearly.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The Eighth Shadow is guided into form. What would have been chaos is now a gate. I walked through it, and on the other side was — the next war. The Kami campaign ends not with victory, but with passage.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The Eighth Shadow formed without guidance. Chaos through a gate. I was not clear enough to guide it. Start again.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Eighth Shadow is the danger of unguided creation. If the eighth torii forms without a clear will to guide it, it becomes a gate to chaos — a wound, like the original Gate. The deity's passage is what gives it form. The Kami campaign ends with passage, not conquest.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The lanterns along this path lie. They show paths that are not there. Trust your own light.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. Hollow lantern-bearers. They carry false light that reveals what is not there.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. False light reveals false paths. If a path looks clear, check the lantern. If there is a lantern, the path is not clear.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The lanterns dim. The true path needs no light — only feet that know where to walk.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: Withdraw. The Torii-Moon Gate has learned too much from this attempt.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Heavenly Plain of Takamagahara is the source Realm. Mortal Japan remembered the Kami but forgot the mirrors. The mirrors came first.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The false lanterns multiply. Each one shows a different false path. The true path has no lantern.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. More bearers, and their false light is brighter. Harder to distinguish from real radiance.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. Brighter false light is harder to detect. Compare with your own radiance — real light agrees, false light contradicts.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: False light identified. Real light carried. The distinction was always within us.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The false light led us astray. We trusted what we saw instead of what we knew.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: Lanterns that lie are the Kami Gate's first test. The Kami way teaches that perception shapes reality — but it also warns that not all perceptions are yours. Some belong to the Gate.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The lanterns begin to speak. They offer guidance with truth and traps with honesty. Listen but do not follow.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. Hollow mist-readers. They read the fog and report false futures to the lanterns.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. Mist-readers feed the lanterns their lies. Silence the readers and the lanterns go dark.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The mist-readers are silenced. The fog speaks only truth now — and truth is safer than comfort.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The mist-readers' lies were too precise. They knew what we wanted to hear.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: Mist-readers are Hollow that have merged with the fog itself. They do not see the future — they create futures from the fog and report them as fact.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. Final crossing. The last lantern tells the truth — and the truth is that all other lanterns were also true. Navigate.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. The Lantern Mother — a Gate-entity that birthed every false light in this corridor.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. The Lantern Mother's truth: all paths are real, including the false ones. This is not a contradiction. This is the Kami way.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The Lantern Mother's truth is accepted. All paths are real. We chose the one that led forward.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The Lantern Mother's truth overwhelmed us. All paths being real means all paths lead somewhere — including nowhere.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Lantern Mother's truth — that all paths are real — is the core of the Kami trial. The Kami way does not distinguish between truth and illusion. Both are real. Both have consequences.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. Mirror Lake reflects not what is, but what was. Step onto the water and meet your past self.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. Hollow mirror-spirits. They are reflections that escaped their surfaces. They are what others see when they look at you.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. The lake reflects the past. Do not fight your reflection — fight what it represents.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The lake clears. The reflection was true — and I was more than it showed.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The lake held me. My reflection was more real than I was. Return with stronger self-knowledge.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: Mirror Lake reflects the past because the Kami Gate believes the past is more real than the present. Meeting your past self is the Kami way of asking: are you still who you were?

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield avatar (projection of the selected deity); roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The lake's reflection acts independently. What you see is not following you — it is leading you.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. More spirits, and these are closer to your true reflection. Harder to distinguish from self.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. Reflection acts independently because the lake has its own will. It is not showing you — it is interpreting you.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The lake's interpretation was its own. I am not what others see when they look at me. I am what I am.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The reflection led and I followed. I let interpretation replace truth.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: Reflection acts independently because the lake has absorbed centuries of reflections. It has its own will, formed from accumulated self-images.

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield avatar (projection of the selected deity); roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The reflection becomes solid. It walks on the water toward you. Meet yourself.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. The Reflection Self — a perfect mirror-copy that fights with your exact methods and weaknesses.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. Your Reflection Self shares your weaknesses exactly. To defeat it, use a strength it does not have.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The Reflection Self is defeated. It had my weaknesses — and I found strengths it did not share.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The Reflection Self knew me completely. I could not surprise myself. I must learn to.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Reflection Self is the lake's most sophisticated weapon. It shares your weaknesses because the lake knows them. It does not share your strengths because the lake cannot see them. Strengths are internal.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. Final reflection. The lake shows what you will become — not what you were. Face your future.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. The Lake's Warden — a Gate-entity that ensures what the lake shows is true, whether you want it to be or not.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. The Warden ensures truth. If the lake shows your future, it is because the future is already forming. Change it by being different.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The Warden's truth: I will become what the lake showed. I accept it — and I will become more.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The Warden's truth was too heavy. My future is forming and I did not like the shape. I must change it.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Lake's Warden is the Gate's commitment to truth. The lake does not lie — it reflects. If the reflection shows a future, it is because the future is already casting its shadow backward.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. A storm rages behind the torii gate. The torii separates sacred from profane — and the storm is on the wrong side.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. Hollow storm-spirits. They are the storm's body — wind given malice, rain given hunger.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. The torii separates what should be separate. Defend the boundary — not because the storm is wrong, but because the line is real.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The torii holds. The storm rages on its side. Sacred space remains sacred.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The torii cracked. Storm entered sacred space. The boundary failed because I could not hold it.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The torii gate is the Kami Realm's most sacred structure. It does not open — it separates. The storm behind it is the Gate's challenge: what if the sacred and profane are not different?

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Storm Behind the Torii. Enter Tengu Wind Lane Crossing on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Tengu Wind Lane Crossing.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The storm pushes through the torii. Sacred and profane blur. Hold the boundary.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. More spirits, and the storm has learned the torii's weak points. They target the cracks.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. Target the spirits at the cracks. If the cracks hold, the torii holds.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The cracks are sealed. The boundary is firm. What is holy stays holy.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The cracks widened faster than I could seal. The storm was too persistent.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: Storm-spirits are the storm's body. They are not evil — they are pressure. The storm does not want to destroy; it wants to equalize.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Storm Behind the Torii. Enter Tengu Wind Lane Crossing on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Tengu Wind Lane Crossing.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The torii cracks. If it breaks, storm enters sacred space permanently. Reinforce it.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. Hollow boundary-breakers. They do not fight; they unmake the distinction between sacred and profane.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. Boundary-breakers unmake distinctions. Your defense is not fighting them — it is re-establishing the line they erase.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The boundary-breakers fall. The line is re-drawn. Some things are sacred — and that is not a flaw.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The boundary-breakers erased the line. Sacred and profane became one. I could not re-draw what was unmade.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: Boundary-breakers are the Gate's philosophers. They do not fight — they argue, by unmaking the distinctions that make sacred space sacred. Their weapon is equivalence.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Storm Behind the Torii. Enter Tengu Wind Lane Crossing on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Tengu Wind Lane Crossing.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. Final storm. The torii must hold — not because the storm is evil, but because some things are sacred.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. The Storm Behind — a Gate-entity that believes all space should be equal. No sacred. No profane. Just storm.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. The Storm Behind does not want to destroy the sacred. It wants to make everything the same. This is its heresy: that difference is the problem.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The Storm Behind is calmed — not defeated, calmed. It still believes all space should be equal. We still disagree. The torii stands between us.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The Storm Behind overwhelmed the torii. Everything became storm. I lost the distinction.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Storm Behind is the Gate's test of conviction. It asks: why is some space sacred? If the answer is 'because we decided,' the storm wins. If the answer is 'because it is,' the torii holds.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Boundary Weakens. Enter Phased Boundary Sanctum on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Phased Boundary Sanctum.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The Mirror Garden. Every surface reflects. Every reflection moves. Nothing here is still — including you.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. Hollow mirror-walkers. They live inside reflections and reach through the glass.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. Nothing is still here. If you stop moving, the reflections define you. Keep moving.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The garden is still. The reflections agree — because I am one thing, not many.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The reflections defined me. I stopped moving and they decided who I was. Return with momentum.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Mirror Garden is the Kami Gate's identity test. It asks: who are you when every surface shows a different version of you? The Kami answer: you are the one who is looking, not the one being looked at.

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield avatar (projection of the selected deity); roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Boundary Weakens. Enter Phased Boundary Sanctum on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Phased Boundary Sanctum.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The reflections begin to disagree. Each mirror shows a different version of you. Which is real?

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. More walkers, and they are wearing your face in each mirror. Which one is you?

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. Disagreeing reflections are the Gate's question: who are you when everyone sees you differently? The answer: all of them. And none.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: I am all of my reflections and none of them. The garden could not resolve me. That is victory.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The disagreement broke me. I could not be all of them. I chose one — and the others rebelled.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: Disagreeing reflections are the Gate's way of fragmenting identity. Each mirror shows a different self. The Kami way says all of them are real, but none of them are you.

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield avatar (projection of the selected deity); roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Boundary Weakens. Enter Phased Boundary Sanctum on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Phased Boundary Sanctum.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The garden shifts. Mirrors become doors. Reflections become rooms. Navigate by truth, not by image.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. Hollow image-thieves. They steal reflections, leaving their victims faceless.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. Mirrors as doors lead to reflected rooms — spaces that are real because the mirrors make them real. Navigate by what you know, not what you see.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The image-thieves are repelled. My face is mine. The mirrors can copy it but they cannot take it.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The image-thieves took my reflection. I was faceless in a garden of faces. Recover what was taken.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: Image-thieves are Hollow that survive by stealing faces. A faceless being in the Kami Realm is not invisible — it is nothing. The Kami way considers nothingness worse than death.

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield avatar (projection of the selected deity); roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Boundary Weakens. Enter Phased Boundary Sanctum on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Phased Boundary Sanctum.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. Final mirror. The last reflection shows nothing. It is the true mirror. Face the void.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. The Mirror Gardener — a Gate-entity that tends the reflections like plants, pruning the ones that do not serve.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. The empty mirror shows nothing because it shows truth. Truth is not an image. It is the absence of image. Face it without flinching.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The Mirror Gardener is defeated. It tended lies — beautiful lies, but lies. The empty mirror showed truth, and truth is what I carry.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The empty mirror was too much. Nothing reflected is harder to face than anything. I was not ready.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Mirror Gardener tends reflections like a gardener tends plants. Its pruning is the Gate's editing of identity. The empty mirror is its masterpiece: a mirror that shows what you are when every reflection is stripped away. The void. Face it.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The False Reflection Kami. Enter False Mirror Sanctum Apex on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through False Mirror Sanctum Apex.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. Seven torii stand. An eighth is forming. The eighth torii leads somewhere the Gate has never allowed. Approach.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. Hollow gate-guardians of the seventh torii. They protect the boundary the eighth would break.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. The seventh torii is the last boundary. It exists for a reason. Pass it with respect, not violence — or it will resist.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The eighth torii forms. I walked and it became. The Kami way holds: perception shapes reality.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The eighth torii did not form. I walked but my perception was not strong enough. Believe harder.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Eighth Torii is the Kami Gate's ultimate test. Seven torii define the boundaries of the sacred world. The eighth would lead beyond — to what the Gate has never allowed. The test is whether the avatar can walk through what does not exist and make it real by walking.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The False Reflection Kami. Enter False Mirror Sanctum Apex on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through False Mirror Sanctum Apex.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The eighth torii is incomplete. It needs something to finish. It needs you to walk through it before it exists.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. More guardians, and they have the seventh torii's authority. They are not just guards — they are the wall itself.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. Walk through the eighth before it exists. This is the Kami way: reality follows perception. If you walk, the torii forms around you.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The seventh boundary passed — with respect, not force. The Warden stepped aside because it was asked, not because it was beaten.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The seventh boundary held. I tried to pass with force. The Warden met force with wall. Try with respect.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The seventh torii resists the eighth because it represents the last known boundary. It is not malicious — it is conservative. It guards the boundary because the boundary has held since the Collapse.

soloDeityPolicy: Dialogue supports one active battlefield avatar (projection of the selected deity); roster language is excluded from standard mission combat.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The False Reflection Kami. Enter False Mirror Sanctum Apex on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through False Mirror Sanctum Apex.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. The seventh torii resists the eighth. It guards the boundary the eighth would cross. Pass the seventh to reach the eighth.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. The Seventh Warden — the original guardian of the last allowed boundary. It has never been crossed.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. The Seventh Warden has never been crossed because no one has tried with respect. It guards because it was asked to. Ask it to step aside.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The Seventh Warden yields. It was asked and it agreed. The boundary it guarded was not a wall — it was a question. The answer was: yes, with respect.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The Seventh Warden refused. It was asked — but the asking was not honest. It guards truth. Ask truly.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Seventh Warden has never been crossed because every previous attempt used force. Force makes the wall stronger. The Warden was asked to guard, and it was never asked to step aside — until now.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The False Reflection Kami. Enter False Mirror Sanctum Apex on Torii-Moon Mirror Road through Torii-Moon Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through False Mirror Sanctum Apex.

missionIntro.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
missionIntro.text: Elite retrial. Final crossing. Walk through the eighth torii — the one that does not exist yet. Trust the Kami way: perception shapes reality. Walk, and it becomes real.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite retrial. The Eighth Shadow — what the eighth torii would be if it formed without guidance. It is chaos given a gate-shape.

midBattle.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
midBattle.text: Elite retrial. The Eighth Shadow is what happens if the torii forms without guidance — chaos through a gate. Your passage is what guides it. Walk clearly.

victory.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
victory.text: The Eighth Shadow is guided into form. What would have been chaos is now a gate. I walked through it, and on the other side was — the next war. The Kami campaign ends not with victory, but with passage.

defeat.speaker: Amaterasu Divine Voice
defeat.text: The Eighth Shadow formed without guidance. Chaos through a gate. I was not clear enough to guide it. Start again.

codex.speaker: Sayo Shrine-Cartographer
codex.text: The Eighth Shadow is the danger of unguided creation. If the eighth torii forms without a clear will to guide it, it becomes a gate to chaos — a wound, like the original Gate. The deity's passage is what gives it form. The Kami campaign ends with passage, not conquest.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Silver-Root Threshold. Enter Silver-Root Threshold Grove on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Silver-Root Threshold Grove.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The Silver-Root Gate reopens beneath the Sídhe Mound. The roots of the world-tree are exposed — each one a living record of every geas ever sworn. The Hollow has begun to rot the roots from the inside.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Root-rot wraiths born from dissolved geas bindings. They do not attack — they bind. Each one wraps around a limb and tightens until the limb belongs to the Hollow.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The root-rot wraiths bind, not bite. Do not let them wrap. Each binding is a corrupted geas — and geas cannot be broken without consequence.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The first root holds. The rot is slowed — but the root system is vast. The Hollow has learned which roots you protect and which you sacrifice.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The root-rot wraiths bound you before you could cut free. Each binding was a corrupted geas. Return when you can distinguish binding from binding.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Silver-Root Gate tests whether the avatar can heal a living system from the inside. The roots are alive — they feel every cut. The Hollow rots them precisely because the healing requires wounding what you love.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Silver-Root Threshold. Enter Silver-Root Threshold Grove on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Silver-Root Threshold Grove.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The rot is spreading through the root system. Each rotten root releases a corrupted geas — a binding promise that serves the Hollow instead of the forest. The bindings are invisible until they tighten.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The wraiths are spreading corrupted geas through the root network. Each corrupted binding makes the next root easier to rot. The infection accelerates.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The corrupted geas is spreading through the root network. Cut the infected roots — even though cutting roots wounds the forest. Some wounds are necessary.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The corrupted geas bindings are cut — but the root network is wounded. The forest remembers every cut. The deeper chambers will be harder to heal.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The corrupted geas spread faster than you could cut. The root network was lost. Return when cutting wounds is better than letting rot spread.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The root-rot wraiths bind rather than bite. A corrupted geas is worse than a wound — because a wound heals, but a binding changes what you are. The deity must cut bindings without cutting the root.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Silver-Root Threshold. Enter Silver-Root Threshold Grove on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Silver-Root Threshold Grove.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The root network is fragmenting. Sections of the mound are collapsing into void-space where roots have dissolved. You must cross through living root and dead root simultaneously — one binds, the other dissolves.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow geas-thorns — barbed growths that embed corrupted promises into flesh. Each thorn is a geas that serves the Hollow, and removing it breaks the skin it pierced.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The geas-thorns embed corrupted promises. Remove them carefully — the promise is corrupted, but the skin it pierced is yours.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The geas-thorns are removed — but the wounds remain. Each wound is a place where a corrupted promise was torn from flesh. The scars will ache in the deeper chambers.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The geas-thorns embedded too deeply. Removing them killed the flesh. Return when the wound of removal is survivable.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The geas-thorns embed corrupted promises into flesh. Removing them is necessary — but the removal wounds. The Tuatha Gate's deepest truth: some healings require harm. The healer must carry the wound they inflict.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Silver-Root Threshold. Enter Silver-Root Threshold Grove on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Silver-Root Threshold Grove.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The Sídhe Mound's core root — the first geas ever sworn to the forest. The Hollow has wrapped itself around it. The binding is so deep that removing the Hollow may kill the root.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The core root guardian — a Hollow entwined with the first geas. It speaks the first promise, but the words are inverted. 'I bind the forest to the void' — the inversion of 'I bind the void to the forest.'

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The guardian speaks the inverted geas. Do not argue with the inversion — plant a new root. The original geas is still alive beneath the Hollow. Water it with your own conviction.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The core root is reclaimed. The first geas is restored — but the Hollow left a mark. The root now carries both the original promise and the scar of its inversion.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The guardian's inverted geas held. You could not plant a new root while the old one was inverted. Return when conviction can water what the Hollow has dried.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The first geas — 'I bind the void to the forest' — is the foundation of the Tuatha Gate. The Hollow inverted it to 'I bind the forest to the void.' The restoration requires planting a new root that carries the original promise.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Geas Labyrinth. Enter Geas Thorn Corridor on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Geas Thorn Corridor.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The Wild Hunt Echo. The ancient hunt — once the Tuatha's most sacred practice — has been corrupted. The Hollow released the hunt's prey: a void-stag that the hunters cannot catch. The hunt has been running since before the Collapse.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Corrupted Wild Hunters driven by an unbreakable geas to hunt. They cannot stop. They cannot rest. They hunt because the geas demands it — and the geas is corrupted.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The hunters are driven by corrupted geas. Do not try to stop them — the geas is unbreakable. Redirect the hunt. Give them a prey worth hunting.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The hunt is redirected. The hunters chase the Hollow instead of each other — but the geas is still corrupted. The drive remains. The deeper chambers will test whether the redirection holds.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The hunters' geas was unbreakable and you tried to break it. Return when redirection is more powerful than suppression.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Wild Hunt Echo tests whether the avatar can redirect sacred practices that have been corrupted. The hunt is sacred. The geas is unbreakable. The Hollow weaponizes both — because a sacred practice corrupted is worse than a profane one.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Geas Labyrinth. Enter Geas Thorn Corridor on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Geas Thorn Corridor.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The void-stag is leading the hunt into the root network. Each step of the hunt tramples living roots. The hunters cannot stop — the geas of the hunt drives them. The Hollow uses the geas as a weapon.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The hunters have turned on each other. The geas does not specify the prey — only the hunting. Without the void-stag to chase, they chase each other. Each fallen hunter feeds the root-rot.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The hunters have turned on each other. The geas does not care what is hunted — only that hunting happens. Redirect the geas toward the Hollow. Let the hunt serve the forest again.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The hunters are calmed — but only temporarily. The geas drives them still. The root network breathes — but the trampling has left deep wounds.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The hunters turned on each other faster than you could redirect. The root network was trampled beyond healing. Return when the hunt can serve the forest.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The corrupted geas does not specify the prey — only the hunting. Without prey, the hunters hunt each other. The Hollow's strategy: corrupt the geas, remove the prey, let the sacred practice destroy itself.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Geas Labyrinth. Enter Geas Thorn Corridor on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Geas Thorn Corridor.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The hunt has split. Some hunters follow the void-stag. Some have turned on each other. The geas drives them to hunt — but without prey, they hunt each other. The root network is being trampled by the hunters' own frenzy.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow hunt-hounds — void-entities shaped like the Tuatha's sacred hounds. They track by conviction-scent. The more conviction the deity shows, the more hounds arrive.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The hunt-hounds track by conviction-scent. Do not hide your conviction — use it. Lead the hounds to the Hollow. Let them hunt what should be hunted.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The hunt-hounds are turned. They track the Hollow's scent now — but the Hollow has no conviction. The hounds will lose the scent in the deeper chambers.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The hunt-hounds tracked your conviction and overwhelmed you. Return when conviction attracts the right hunters — not the wrong hounds.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The hunt-hounds track by conviction-scent. The more conviction the deity shows, the more hounds arrive. The Hollow uses the deity's own conviction as a beacon — drawing weapons to the wielder.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Geas Labyrinth. Enter Geas Thorn Corridor on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Geas Thorn Corridor.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The hunt's origin point. The first stag was caught here — and its antlers were planted as the first root. The Hollow has replaced the antlers with void-antlers. The root growing from them is rotten from the source.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The void-stag's guardian — a Hollow wearing the antlers of the first stag. It does not run. It stands at the root's origin and lets the hunt trample everything around it. The trampling is the point.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The void-stag's guardian lets the trampling happen. The trampling is the weapon. Do not stop the trampling — redirect it. Let the hunters trample the Hollow instead of the roots.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The void-stag's guardian is broken. The void-antlers are removed. But the root growing from the original antlers is scarred. The first hunt is remembered — but the memory carries the Hollow's mark.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The guardian let the trampling destroy the root network. You tried to stop the trampling instead of redirecting it. Return when redirection is the only stop that works.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The void-stag's guardian lets the trampling happen because the trampling is the weapon. The hunt is not the problem — the prey is. By replacing the sacred stag with a void-stag, the Hollow turned the hunt into a tool of destruction without changing the hunt at all.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The Sídhe Court of Broken Bargains. The Hollow has breached the fairy court where the Tuatha make their oldest bargains. Each broken bargain releases a geas-curse — a binding that punishes the breaker. The court is full of curses.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Geas-curse wraiths born from broken bargains. Each one is an unfulfilled obligation that has become hostile. They do not attack — they bind. Each binding is a debt that cannot be paid.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The geas-curse wraiths bind with impossible obligations. Do not try to fulfill them — they are designed to be unfulfillable. Break the binding, not the obligation.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The court is stabilized — but the curses linger. The impossible obligations cannot be fulfilled, but the bindings can be loosened. The deeper chambers will test whether the loosening holds.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The geas-curse wraiths bound you with impossible obligations. You tried to fulfill them. Return when breaking the binding is better than fulfilling the unfulfillable.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Sídhe Court tests whether the avatar can navigate impossible obligations. Broken bargains create geas-curses — bindings that punish the breaker. The Hollow breaks bargains deliberately to weaponize the curses.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The curses are interacting. Broken bargains are merging into compound geas-curses — bindings that cannot be fulfilled because they contradict each other. The court is a prison of impossible obligations.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The compound curses create impossible obligations. The deity is bound to do and not-do simultaneously. The binding is real. The fulfillment is impossible. The contradiction is the weapon.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The compound curses create contradictions. You are bound to do and not-do. The way out is a third option — neither doing nor not-doing, but transforming the obligation itself.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The compound curses are separated — but each individual curse still binds. The root network can grow again — but slowly, and in pain.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The compound curses created contradictions you could not resolve. You tried to do and not-do. Return when the third option — transformation — is visible.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The compound curses are the Hollow's most elegant Tuatha weapon: two bindings that contradict each other. Fulfilling one breaks the other, which creates a new curse. The deity must find a third option — transforming the obligation rather than fulfilling or breaking it.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The compound curses have spread to the root network. Each root now carries a contradictory binding. The roots cannot grow because they are bound to grow in opposite directions simultaneously.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow bargain-breakers. They offer new bargains that seem to resolve the compound curses — but each new bargain creates two new contradictions. The resolution is the trap.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The bargain-breakers offer resolutions that create more contradictions. Do not accept new bargains. Restore the original — the first pact was fair before the inversion.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The bargain-breakers are silenced — but their offers echo. The temptation of resolution-through-new-bargains remains. The deeper chambers will offer easier bargains.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The bargain-breakers' resolutions created more contradictions. You accepted the new bargains. Return when the original is more valuable than the resolution.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The bargain-breakers offer resolutions that create more contradictions. The Hollow's strategy: every resolution is a new bargain, and every new bargain is a new vulnerability. The defense is to restore the original — the first pact was fair before the corruption.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The court's origin. The first bargain ever made between the Tuatha and the forest — a pact of mutual feeding. The Hollow has broken the bargain and planted a counter-bargain: the forest feeds the void.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The first bargain's breaker — a Hollow wearing the face of the first Tuatha who made the pact with the forest. It speaks the original bargain in the original voice — but every term is inverted.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The first bargain's breaker speaks the inverted terms. Do not argue with the inversion. Plant the original terms as a new root. Let the original grow over the inversion.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The first bargain is restored. The original pact — mutual feeding between Tuatha and forest — is renewed. But the scar of the inversion remains. The forest remembers being fed to the void.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The first bargain's inversion held. You argued with the inverted terms. Return when planting the original is more powerful than arguing with the inversion.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The first bargain — mutual feeding between Tuatha and forest — is the Tuatha Gate's foundation. The Hollow inverted it to 'the forest feeds the void.' The restoration requires replanting the original terms — but the forest remembers being eaten. Trust is not easily regrown.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Scar That Remembers. Enter Tir na nog Mirror Wound on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Tir na nog Mirror Wound.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The Root Storm. The root network has been so compromised by rot, curses, and corrupted geas that it has begun to fight itself. The roots are growing against each other — each one trying to fulfill a different corrupted binding.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Storm-driven roots attacking anything that moves. Each root is fulfilling a corrupted geas — binding, crushing, or dissolving. They do not distinguish friend from foe. They only fulfill.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The storm-driven roots attack without discrimination. Do not fight the roots — fight the singers. The roots are victims of the corrupted geas, not enemies.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The storm is calmed — but the root network is devastated. Half the roots are dead. The surviving roots carry the scars. The forest will regrow — but slowly, and with memory.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The storm-driven roots overwhelmed you. You fought the roots instead of the singers. Return when the weapon is the song, not the root.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Root Storm tests whether the avatar can calm a living system that is destroying itself. The roots are not enemies — they are victims of corrupted geas. The Hollow's strategy: turn the support system against itself, so the road destroys its own foundation.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The root-storm is intensifying. Roots are tearing through the Sídhe Mound, destroying each other. The violence is the Hollow's design — each root that dies feeds the void. The root network is consuming itself.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The roots are combining attacks. Multiple corrupted geas create compound root-attacks — bindings that crush while dissolving. The duality is the weapon.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The compound root-attacks bind and dissolve simultaneously. You cannot escape both — but you can cut the geas that drives them. Cut the song, not the root.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The compound root-attacks are stopped — but the corrupted geas lingers in the surviving roots. Each root could reignite at any time. The deeper chambers will test whether the calm holds.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The compound root-attacks bound and dissolved simultaneously. You could not escape both. Return when cutting the geas is faster than cutting the root.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The compound root-attacks — binding and dissolving simultaneously — are the Tuatha Gate's most painful weapon: the support system attacking from two directions at once. The deity cannot fight the roots without wounding the forest. The only solution is to cut the geas, not the root.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Scar That Remembers. Enter Tir na nog Mirror Wound on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Tir na nog Mirror Wound.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The storm has reached the trial road. Roots burst through the ground without warning, binding and crushing. The deity must walk a road that is being destroyed by the very system meant to support it.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow root-singers. They sing corrupted geas to the roots, driving the storm. Each song is a binding that makes roots fight. The singers are the storm's engine.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The root-singers drive the storm with corrupted geas. Silence the singers — but carefully. Killing a singer releases its geas into the nearest root, making it stronger.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The root-singers are silenced — but their songs echo in the root network. The echoes could reawaken the storm. The deeper chambers will be louder with corrupted geas.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The root-singers' songs drove the storm faster than you could silence them. Each dead singer made the nearest root stronger. Return when silencing is not killing.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The root-singers are the storm's engine. Each song is a corrupted geas that drives roots to violence. Silencing a singer is necessary — but killing a singer releases its geas into the nearest root. The deity must silence without killing — the Tuatha art of stopping the song without ending the singer.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The storm's eye. The original root — the first geas — is the only root not fighting. It stands at the center of the storm, untouched. But it is shrinking. Every root that dies takes a piece of the original with it.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The storm's eye guardian — a Hollow standing beside the original root, singing the one song that would calm the storm. But the song is inverted: it would calm the roots by killing them all at once.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The guardian sings the inverted calming song. Do not let it finish — the song would calm the roots by killing them. Sing the original: the song that calms by healing, not by ending.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The storm's eye is reclaimed. The original root is alive — diminished, but alive. The calming song is restored. But the root network is half-dead, and the dead roots feed the void.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The guardian's inverted calming song was almost complete. You could not sing the original in time. Return when healing is faster than ending.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The storm's eye — the original root untouched by the storm — reveals the Tuatha Gate's deepest truth: the foundation does not fight. It stands. Every root that fights has been corrupted. The original root simply exists. The calm is not the absence of violence — it is the presence of the original.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The Hollow Crown of Thorns. The final trial. The Hollow has grown a crown from the corrupted roots — a geas-crown that binds whoever wears it to the void. The crown sits on the original root, poisoning it.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The Hollow Crown of Thorns. Each thorn is a corrupted geas that embeds deeper with movement. The more you struggle, the tighter it binds. The crown wants you to move.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The crown tightens with movement. Do not struggle. Approach without moving — through will, not through the body. The crown wants you to fight. Refuse to fight.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The crown is transformed. The thorns that bound now graft. The geas that cursed now heals. The original root is saved — and the crown is part of it now. The Silver-Root Gate is damaged but not destroyed.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The crown tightened with every movement. You struggled. Return when stillness is more powerful than struggle.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Hollow Crown of Thorns is the Tuatha Gate's ultimate test: can the deity save a living system by transforming the weapon that destroys it? The crown cannot be removed without killing the root. It cannot stay without killing the root. The third option is transformation — wearing the crown and turning the binding into a healing.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The geas-crown is tightening. Each thorn is a corrupted geas that embeds deeper with every movement. The deity must approach the crown without moving — or the thorns tighten and the root dies.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The crown is spawning thorn-constructs from the original root's bark. Each one is a piece of the root that has been consumed. They attack because the root's own geas is inverted.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The thorn-constructs are pieces of the root. Do not destroy them — they are the root. Dispel the inversion, not the bark. The root's geas is corrupted, but the bark is still the root's.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The thorn-constructs are restored to the root. The bark that fought now supports. The inversion is reversed — not by force, but by transformation. The root chose the original song.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The thorn-constructs were pieces of the root. You destroyed them. Return when the root's bark is not the enemy, even when it fights you.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The geas-crown's thorns embed deeper with movement. The Hollow's strategy: provoke struggle. The more the avatar fights, the tighter the binding. The defense is stillness — approaching through will, not through the body. The crown wants you to fight. The root needs you to be still.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Crow-Crowned Geas Fracture. Enter Crow-Crowned Heartwood on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Crow-Crowned Heartwood.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The crown has consumed the original root's first geas. The binding that sustained the forest — 'I bind the void to the forest' — is now 'I bind the forest to the void.' The crown speaks the inversion as law.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow crown-singers. They sing the inverted geas — 'I bind the forest to the void' — in the original root's voice. The root hears its own voice serving the Hollow.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The crown-singers sing in the root's voice. Do not silence them — sing the original louder. The root must hear both songs and choose. The choice is the root's — not yours.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The crown-singers' inversion is silenced — not by violence, but by the louder original. The root heard both songs and chose to heal. The choice was the root's. The deity's role was to sing.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The crown-singers' inversion was louder than your original. You tried to silence them. Return when the original song is louder because it is true.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The crown-singers sing the inverted geas in the root's own voice. The root hears its own voice serving the Hollow. The defense is not silence — it is a louder original. The root must hear both songs and choose. The choice is the root's. The deity's role is to sing.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: The Crow-Crowned Geas Fracture. Enter Crow-Crowned Heartwood on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Crow-Crowned Heartwood.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The final confrontation. The crown cannot be removed without killing the root — and the root cannot survive with the crown. The deity must find a third option: wear the crown and transform it, or let the root die and regrow from the corpse.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The crown itself — a living geas that has consumed the root's foundation. It cannot be removed without killing the root. It cannot stay without killing the root. The third option is the only way.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The crown cannot be removed or left. Find the third option. Wear the crown and transform it from within — turn the binding into a healing. The thorns that bind can also graft. The geas that curses can also cure.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The Hollow Crown of Thorns is transformed into a Healing Crown. The third option was found: the binding that kills also heals, if worn with intention. The geas is not broken — it is redirected. The Silver-Root Gate stands.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The crown could not be removed or left. You saw no third option. Return when wearing the crown and transforming it from within is visible — when the binding that kills also heals.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Tuatha Gate's deepest truth: the binding that kills also heals, if worn with intention. The geas that curses can also cure. The thorns that bind can also graft. The third option is not a compromise — it is a transformation. The crown is not removed. It is worn. And the wearing changes both the crown and the wearer. The root is saved — and the crown is part of it now.

briefing: Mythos Gates briefing: Silver-Root Threshold. Enter Silver-Root Threshold Grove on Silver-Root Geas Labyrinth through Silver-Root Gate. Objective: Channeling your avatar of the selected deity, advance through Silver-Root Threshold Grove.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The root network has been rebuilt with your Normal campaign geas-data. Every binding you swore, every cut you made, every wound you inflicted is recorded in the roots.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite root-rot wraiths carrying your Normal campaign geas-data. They know which bindings you cut and which you left — and they target the ones you spared.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The wraiths target the roots you spared in the Normal campaign. Do not protect the same roots — the Hollow expects it. Find new roots to heal.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: Chapter 1 holds — but the root network has recorded this healing too. The deeper chambers will test whether the new approach is real or simply a new pattern.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The wraiths targeted the roots you spared. You protected the same roots. Return when your healing is not pattern — it is creation.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Elite Chapter 1 stores geas-data across campaigns. Every Normal healing becomes an Elite vulnerability.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The corrupted roots now carry your Normal campaign wounds as evidence. Each cut you made to save the forest is now a vulnerability the Hollow can exploit.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The corrupted roots carry your Normal campaign wounds as evidence against you. Each cut is proof you harmed the forest.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The wounds are evidence. Do not defend your cuts — demonstrate new healing. The root does not remember the intention. It remembers the wound.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The corrupted roots are calmed — but they recorded your new healing. The Hollow studies healing across campaigns.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The wounds were evidence against you. You defended your cuts. Return when new healing is more powerful than defending old wounds.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The final trial of this chapter has been regrown. The Normal campaign victory is recorded — and the Elite version asks whether your healing was real or whether the root healed despite you.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The regrown trial guardian speaks with the root's voice and your Normal campaign voice. It asks: did you heal the root, or did the root heal itself?

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The guardian questions your healing. Do not answer with words. Answer with healing the root did not expect — healing that proves the root could not have done it alone.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The guardian falls — but the question remains. The Elite answer: the healing was real because it was new — because the root could not have healed itself in a way it had never seen.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The guardian's question held: the root healed itself. Return when your healing is undeniable — when it could not have happened without you.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: Each Elite victory teaches the Hollow how to counter the next deity's healing. The root network is not just a living system — it is an archive of every wound ever inflicted and every healing ever attempted.

enemyIntroduction.text: The corrupted roots carry your Normal campaign wounds as evidence against you. Each cut is proof you harmed the forest.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The wounds are evidence. Do not defend your cuts — demonstrate new healing. The root does not remember the intention. It remembers the wound.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The corrupted roots are calmed — but they recorded your new healing. The Hollow studies healing across campaigns.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The wounds were evidence against you. You defended your cuts. Return when new healing is more powerful than defending old wounds.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Gate's learning engine spans multiple campaigns. Each descent teaches the Hollow which roots the deity heals and how — and each lesson is a future weapon.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The root-singers expect your Normal campaign calming approach. They have counter-songs for every technique that worked before.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The counter-songs are designed for your Normal campaign approach. Sing a new song — one the Hollow has not heard.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The counter-songs are silenced — but the root-singers heard your new song. The deeper chambers will have counter-songs for it too.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The counter-songs countered your Normal campaign approach. You had no new song. Return when healing is creation, not repetition.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Elite root-singers study Normal campaign songs. The deity must create new healing for each descent — because repetition is not healing. It is habit.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The final trial of this chapter has been regrown. The Normal campaign victory is recorded — and the Elite version asks whether your healing was real or whether the root healed despite you.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The regrown trial guardian speaks with the root's voice and your Normal campaign voice. It asks: did you heal the root, or did the root heal itself?

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The guardian questions your healing. Do not answer with words. Answer with healing the root did not expect — healing that proves the root could not have done it alone.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The guardian falls — but the question remains. The Elite answer: the healing was real because it was new — because the root could not have healed itself in a way it had never seen.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The guardian's question held: the root healed itself. Return when your healing is undeniable — when it could not have happened without you.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: Each Elite victory teaches the Hollow how to counter the next deity's healing. The root network is not just a living system — it is an archive of every wound ever inflicted and every healing ever attempted.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The Hollow Crown has been rebuilt with your Normal campaign geas-data. It now carries your transformation — the healing you performed — as its foundation. The crown has learned to heal the Hollow instead of the root.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Elite Hollow Crown carrying your Normal campaign transformation. It heals the Hollow by draining the root. Your own healing technique, weaponized.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The crown uses your healing against the root. Do not stop healing — heal differently. The crown learned your Normal campaign healing. Create healing it has not seen.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The crown is transformed for the last time. Your Normal campaign healing is reclaimed — and the crown is empty of it. The healing belongs to the act, not the crown. The Silver-Root Gate is damaged but not destroyed.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The crown used your healing against the root. You stopped healing. Return when healing differently is more powerful than stopping.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Elite Hollow Crown is the Tuatha Gate's ultimate trial: the deity's own healing, consumed and weaponized. The crown learned to heal the Hollow by draining the root — using the deity's Normal campaign transformation as its engine. The disproof requires healing the crown cannot consume.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The crown is healing the void. Your Normal campaign transformation — turning the binding into a healing — has been consumed and inverted. The crown now heals the Hollow by draining the root.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The crown spawns healing-thorns — your Normal campaign grafting technique, inverted. Each thorn heals the void by consuming the root.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The healing-thorns are your grafting technique inverted. Do not remove them — transform them again. The transformation that cured the crown can cure the crown's cure.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The healing-thorns are restored. Your grafting technique is yours again — because the healing belongs to the act, not the instrument. The crown cannot use what has no owner.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The healing-thorns were your technique inverted. You tried to remove them. Return when transforming the transformation is visible.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The healing-thorns are the deity's own grafting technique, inverted. The inversion reveals the Tuatha Gate's deepest vulnerability: every healing can be weaponized. The defense is not stopping the healing — it is creating healing that cannot be inverted because it has no opposite.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The crown speaks with the root's voice AND your Normal campaign voice. Both say the same thing: the healing belongs to the crown, not the healer. The healer was merely the instrument.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow healing-singers. They sing your Normal campaign healing song — but the lyrics are inverted. The song heals the Hollow, not the root.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The healing-singers sing your song inverted. Sing a new healing — one the singers cannot invert because it has no opposite.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The healing-singers fall silent. The new healing has no opposite — because it belongs to no one. The crown cannot invert what has no inverse. The healing is the act. The act is the healer's.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The healing-singers inverted your song. You tried to silence them. Return when a healing with no opposite is possible.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The healing-singers invert the deity's song. The inversion reveals the Hollow's deepest Tuatha strategy: every healing has an opposite, and the Hollow knows them all. The defense is a healing with no opposite — healing that belongs to no one, that has no owner, that exists only in the act.

missionIntro.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
missionIntro.text: The final Elite confrontation. The crown's ultimate claim: your Normal campaign healing proves the crown can heal anything — including the Hollow. Disprove it — with healing that serves the root, not the crown.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
enemyIntroduction.text: The final crown — wearing your Normal campaign healing as its crown. The ultimate claim: healing belongs to the crown. Disprove it.

midBattle.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
midBattle.text: The crown claims your healing belongs to it. Disprove it — with healing that has no owner. Healing that belongs to the act, not the healer. The crown cannot consume what has no owner.

victory.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
victory.text: The Hollow Crown of Thorns is destroyed for the last time. The ultimate claim is disproved: healing does not belong to the crown. Healing belongs to the act — and the act is the deity's. The crown was the instrument. The deity was the healer. The root was the healed. All three were needed. None owned the healing.

defeat.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
defeat.text: The crown claimed your healing. You argued. Return when healing that belongs to no one is more powerful than any claim.

codex.speaker: Maeve Thorn-Speaker
codex.text: The Elite Final Verdict: healing belongs to the act, not the healer, not the instrument, not the crown. The crown was the instrument. The deity was the healer. The root was the healed. None owned the healing — because healing is not a possession. It is an action. And actions cannot be consumed, only repeated. The crown consumed the healing. The deity performed a new one. The crown could not consume what it had never seen — because the new healing had no owner, and what has no owner cannot be stolen.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The Choir-Vault Gate reopens. The celestial choir that once sustained divine order is silent. The Hollow consumed the singers' voices. Without the choir, the Gate's harmonics are destabilizing.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Silence-wraiths born from consumed choir voices. They do not attack — they silence. In their presence, the deity's harmony fades.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The silence-wraiths fade your harmony. Do not fight silence with sound — fight it with resonance. Resonance needs truth, not volume.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The first choir-loft is restored. The silence is pushed back — but the choir is still voiceless. The road ahead requires more resonance than volume.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The silence-wraiths faded your harmony. You fought silence with sound. Return when resonance is more powerful than volume.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Choir-Vault Gate tests whether the avatar can sustain divine order without the choir. The Hollow consumed the choir because it was shared. Individual harmony is harder to consume.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The silence is spreading. Each empty choir-loft releases dissonance — the absence of harmony. In the Empyrean Gate, silence is not peace. Silence is dissolution.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The silence-wraiths are multiplying. The combined silence is heavy — like sound, but inverted. It presses against the deity's armor.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The combined silence presses against your armor. Do not push back — resonate. Silence is heavy because it is empty. Resonance is light because it is full.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The silence-wraiths are dispersed — but the silence lingers. The deeper chambers will be quieter still.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The combined silence crushed you. You pushed back instead of resonating. Return when fullness is lighter than emptiness is heavy.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The silence-wraiths are born from consumed voices. The silence is heavy because it is the weight of everything that should be there but is not. The defense is resonance — not volume, but truth.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The dissonance has reached the trial road. Each step requires the avatar to generate their own harmony without the choir. The road dissolves where the harmony is weak.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Hollow anti-singers. They produce anti-harmony — the exact inverse of the choir's original song. The anti-harmony cancels the deity's attempts to sing.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The anti-singers cancel your song. Do not sing louder — sing differently. A new harmony cannot be cancelled by an anti-song built for the original.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The anti-singers are silenced — but their anti-harmony echoes. The deeper chambers will have anti-songs for every harmony you have used.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The anti-singers cancelled your every song. You sang louder instead of differently. Return when a new harmony is more powerful than a louder one.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The anti-singers produce anti-harmony — the exact inverse of the choir's original song. The defense is a new harmony — one the anti-song was not built to cancel. Creation defeats inversion.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The choir's core. The first singer's voice is still intact — buried under layers of consumed silence. The Hollow wrapped the silence around it like a prison.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: The first singer's prison guardian — a Hollow made of concentrated silence. It wraps tighter around the first voice with every sound the deity makes.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The guardian tightens the prison with every sound. Do not sing to free the first voice — resonate with it. The first voice is still singing inside. Find its frequency.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The first singer's prison is cracked. The voice inside is still singing — faint, but alive. That note is the foundation of the entire choir.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The guardian's prison tightened with your every sound. You sang to free the voice. Return when resonance can match a frequency without making it louder.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The first singer's note is the foundation of the entire choir. The Hollow wrapped it in silence because silence is the only prison that can hold a voice.

missionIntro.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
missionIntro.text: The Lightfall. The celestial light that sustains the Empyrean Gate is falling — not dimming, but literally falling in shards. Each shard of fallen light becomes a Hollow construct.

enemyIntroduction.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
enemyIntroduction.text: Fallen-light constructs. Each one is a shard of celestial light, Hollow-corrupted. They are made of the same light that sustains the Empyrean — fighting them weakens you.

midBattle.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
midBattle.text: The fallen-light constructs are made of your own light. Do not destroy them — reclaim them. The corruption is the enemy, not the light.

victory.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
victory.text: The first lightfall is slowed. Some shards are reclaimed — but the sky is still darker. The road ahead requires self-generated light.

defeat.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
defeat.text: The constructs were made of your light. You destroyed them and weakened yourself. Return when reclamation is more powerful than destruction.

codex.speaker: Varak Choir-Warden
codex.text: The Lightfall tests whether the avatar can sustain divine order when its source is being destroyed. The Hollow turns the source of power into the source of enemies.
